title: Scenario Planning Software Feature Comparison for Replacing Legacy EPM: Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Oracle EPM, Pigment and More (2026)
summary: Compare Abacum, Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Oracle EPM, Pigment and Planful on six scenario planning features to check before replacing legacy EPM.
body_markdown:
*Last updated November 18, 2026*


When you replace a legacy EPM tool such as Oracle Hyperion, the scenario planning features that matter most are scenario versioning, driver-based logic, approval workflows with an audit trail, spreadsheet connectivity, governed AI and finance-owned maintenance. Abacum, Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Oracle EPM, Pigment and Planful all cover scenario planning, and they differ most in who builds and maintains the models.


## Key takeaways


-


Replatforming changes the feature checklist. You are moving logic, history and approvals, so migration support matters as much as the feature list.


-


Compare platforms on six features: scenario versioning, driver-based logic, approvals and audit trail, spreadsheet connectivity, governed AI, and who maintains the model.


-


Ask each vendor to run one of your real scenarios live and to show how the result traces back to its inputs.


-


Use our[scenario planning software compared](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/scenario-planning-software-comparison) guide alongside this one for a platform-by-platform view.


## The six features to compare


Feature


What to confirm in the demo


Scenario versioning


Can you branch, name, compare and archive scenarios without copying files?


Driver-based logic


Can finance add or change a driver without a ticket, and does the change flow through the whole plan?


Approvals and audit trail


Does every change to a reported figure have an owner, an approval and a record?


Spreadsheet connectivity


Can existing spreadsheet models come in, and can plan work go back out to a spreadsheet?


Governed AI


Does every AI-generated number trace to source data and assumptions, and does finance approve it?


Model ownership


Who builds, changes and maintains models after go-live?

### Oracle EPM


Oracle EPM is Oracle's enterprise performance management suite, and Oracle Hyperion is the lineage many legacy planning programs started from. **Best for:** teams that are deeply invested in the Oracle ecosystem. **Ask:** What does the move from Hyperion look like for our logic, our dimensions and our reports?


### Anaplan


Anaplan is a long-standing enterprise connected planning platform, known for its Hyperblock engine, extensive modeling and a large template ecosystem. **Best for:** large planning programs with dedicated model builders. **Ask:** Who builds and maintains the models after go-live?


### Workday Adaptive Planning


Workday Adaptive Planning is part of the Workday ecosystem. **Best for:** teams already running Workday for HR and financials. **Ask:** How does it connect to sources outside Workday?


### Pigment


Pigment is a flexible modeling platform for teams that want to design and maintain their own planning models. Your team or an implementation partner designs it and keeps it running. **Best for:** teams that want to design custom models. **Ask:** Who owns the model after go-live?


### Planful


Planful brings planning, reporting and close workflows together for finance teams. **Best for:** teams that want those workflows under one roof. **Ask:** How does a scenario change flow through to reports?

## What replatforming adds to the comparison


Legacy EPM programs carry years of embedded logic, approval chains and report definitions. Before you compare features, list the scenarios leadership asks for most often, the approvals your auditors rely on and the reports that must match on day one. Then ask each vendor how those move, which parts get rebuilt, and how a parallel run works.
